bands.title: Rarely bothered
bands.summary: Your answers suggest anxiety-related experiences have rarely bothered you over the last two weeks.

bands.title: Sometimes bothered
bands.summary: Your answers suggest worry, tension or nervousness have sometimes bothered you recently.

bands.title: Often bothered
bands.summary: Your answers suggest anxiety-related experiences have often affected you over the last two weeks.

bands.title: Very often bothered
bands.summary: Your answers suggest anxiety-related experiences have affected you on most days recently.

support.text: If worry or nervousness is affecting your daily life, sleep or relationships, consider speaking with a doctor or mental health professional. You don't have to manage it alone.

worry.low: Worry and overthinking rarely take over your thoughts.
worry.moderate: Worry and overthinking show up sometimes, often around particular situations.
worry.high: Worrying and replaying things in your mind seem to take up a lot of your time.
worry.reflect: Which worries come back most often, and are they within your control?
worry.tip: Try setting a short "worry time" each day and postponing worries until then.

nervousness.low: You rarely feel on edge in everyday situations.
nervousness.moderate: You sometimes feel nervous or uneasy, often in particular situations.
nervousness.high: Feeling on edge or uneasy seems to happen often for you.
nervousness.reflect: In which situations do you feel most on edge?
nervousness.tip: Before a nerve-racking task, try slow breathing: in for 4, out for 6, a few times.

tension.low: Stress rarely shows up in your body.
tension.moderate: Stress sometimes shows up as tension, aches or a racing heart.
tension.high: Stress often shows up physically, such as tight muscles, headaches or a racing heart.
tension.reflect: Where in your body do you notice stress first?
tension.tip: A few minutes of stretching, or relaxing your shoulders and jaw, can ease built-up tension.

relaxing.low: You can usually switch off and settle.
relaxing.moderate: Relaxing is sometimes hard, especially when you are busy.
relaxing.high: Switching off, resting or sleeping seems difficult for you at the moment.
relaxing.tip: Create a short, screen-free wind-down routine before bed.

apprehension.moderate: You sometimes worry that something bad will happen.
apprehension.high: A sense of dread or expecting bad news seems to visit you often.
apprehension.reflect: When you expect the worst, how often does it actually happen?
apprehension.tip: When dread appears, name it ("this is anxiety talking") and focus on the next small step.

stress.low: Stress rarely affects your mood or focus.
stress.moderate: Stress sometimes leaves you irritable, overwhelmed or distracted.
stress.high: Stress often affects your mood, patience and concentration.
stress.reflect: What are the early signs that stress is building up for you?
stress.tip: Break overwhelming tasks into the smallest possible next step.

suggestions: Regular movement, enough sleep and time outdoors all support a calmer body and mind.
Talking about worries with someone you trust can make them feel smaller.
Notice patterns: when, where and around whom anxiety shows up most.
note: Your score is the average of all 25 answers, shown on a 0–100 scale (0 = not at all, 100 = nearly every day). It combines the 7 GAD-7 questions with 18 MindCheck questions, so it is not a GAD-7 score and cannot indicate an anxiety disorder.
